messages.subject: Running MCMC chains on multiple cores.
messages.subject_clean: Running MCMC chains on multiple cores.
messages.body_plain:
I was wondering if it is possible to run MCMC chains on more than one core per chain. I tried:
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
 I am updated to R version 4.3.2. Sean Anderson has given me these reproducible examples:

library(RTMB)
set.seed(123)
data <- list(Y = rnorm(10) + 1:10, x=1:10)
parameters <- list(a=0, b=0, logSigma=0)

f <- function(parms) {
Y <- data$Y
x <- data$x
a <- parms$a
b <- parms$b
logSigma <- parms$logSigma
ADREPORT(exp(2*logSigma));
nll = -sum(dnorm(Y, a+b*x, exp(logSigma), TRUE))
nll
}
obj <- MakeADFun(f, parameters)

library(tmbstan)
s <- tmbstan(obj, iter = 100, chains = 2, cores = 1) # works
s <- tmbstan(obj, iter = 100, chains = 2, cores = 2) # doesn’t work
  s <- tmbstan(obj, iter = 100, chains = 2, cores = 3) # doesn’t work

Also this ran for Sean, but not for me:
TMB::runExample("simple")
fit <- tmbstan(obj, chains=2, iter = 50, cores = 2) # works

messages.body_plain:
Sarah, I can reproduce your RTMB example on a Windows machine, however the 'simple' TMB example seems to work fine (?). Note, that parallelization works fundamentally different on Windows than other OSes, so the following diagnostics are Windows specific.

1) First problem is that library(RTMB) is not automatically loaded on the nodes. We can fix this by adding 'require(RTMB)' to the body of the function.
2) Second problem is that 'data' is not exported to the nodes. We can fix this using closures, i.e. by explicitly assigning data to evironment(f).

Ideally, these problems should be fixed in the tmbstan package, but for now one must do something like this:

library(RTMB)
set.seed(123)
data <- list(Y = rnorm(10) + 1:10, x=1:10)
parameters <- list(a=0, b=0, logSigma=0)
f <- function(parms) {

  require(RTMB)

  Y <- data$Y
  x <- data$x
  a <- parms$a
  b <- parms$b
  logSigma <- parms$logSigma
  ADREPORT(exp(2*logSigma));
  nll = -sum(dnorm(Y, a+b*x, exp(logSigma), TRUE))
  nll
}

environment(f) <- new.env()
environment(f)$data <- data

obj <- MakeADFun(f, parameters)
library(tmbstan)

s <- tmbstan(obj, iter = 100, chains = 2, cores = 2) ## Works !

messages.subject: Re: Running MCMC chains on multiple cores.
messages.subject_clean: Running MCMC chains on multiple cores.
messages.body_plain:
Yes, multiple threads per chain has worked in TMB for a long time via the 'parallel_accumulator'. In RTMB the parallel split can be fully automated. However, currently the parallel version of RTMB is shipped under a different name 'RTMBp'.
You'll need a fairly large dataset to get a significant speedup, something like:

library(RTMBp)
n <- 1e6
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(n)
data <- list(Y = rnorm(n) + x, x=x)

parameters <- list(a=0, b=0, logSigma=0)
f <- function(parms) {
  Y <- data$Y
  x <- data$x
  a <- parms$a
  b <- parms$b
  logSigma <- parms$logSigma
  ADREPORT(exp(2*logSigma));
  nll = -sum(dnorm(Y, a+b*x, exp(logSigma), TRUE))
  nll
}

obj <- MakeADFun(f, parameters) ## NOTE 'Autopar work split' info on how much work is assigned to each thread
library(tmbstan)
system.time(s <- tmbstan(obj, iter = 1e2, chains = 1,seed=1))

messages.subject: ifelse/if in RTMB
messages.body_plain:
Dear all, I wrote a likelihood function (see code below) and when I use the MakeADFun function from the RTMB package, I got the following error: "Comparison is generally unsafe for AD types"

The comparison is done using ifelse to avoid having to do the log of zero value. Is there a way to overcome this issue?

Thanks

cBhalfnormlike <- function(parm, nXvar, nuZUvar, nvZVvar, nbZBvar, uHvar, vHvar,
  bHvar, Yvar, Xvar, S, wHvar) {
  beta <- parm[1:(nXvar)]
  delta <- parm[(nXvar + 1):(nXvar + nuZUvar)]
  phi <- parm[(nXvar + nuZUvar + 1):(nXvar + nuZUvar + nvZVvar)]
  kappa <- parm[(nXvar + nuZUvar + nvZVvar + 1):(nXvar + nuZUvar + nvZVvar + nbZBvar)]
  Wu <- crossprod(matrix(delta), t(uHvar))[1, ]
  Wv <- crossprod(matrix(phi), t(vHvar))[1, ]
  B <- exp(crossprod(matrix(kappa), t(bHvar))[1, ])
  epsilon <- Yvar - crossprod(matrix(beta), t(Xvar))[1, ]
  mustar <- (-exp(Wu) * S * epsilon)/(exp(Wu) + exp(Wv))
  sigmastar <- sqrt(exp(Wu) * exp(Wv)/(exp(Wu) + exp(Wv)))
  pnoV1 <- pnorm((B - mustar)/sigmastar)
  pnoV2 <- pnorm(-mustar/sigmastar)
  pnoRet <- ifelse(pnoV1 - pnoV2 > 1e-323, pnoV1 - pnoV2, 1e-323)
  ll <- -log(pnorm(B/exp(Wu/2)) - 1/2) - 1/2 * log(exp(Wu) + exp(Wv)) + dnorm(epsilon/sqrt(exp(Wu) +
    exp(Wv)), log = TRUE) + log(pnoRet)
  RTMB::ADREPORT(ll * wHvar)
  return(sum(ll * wHvar))
}

messages.subject: Re: ifelse/if in RTMB
messages.body_plain:
It's not completely settled in RTMB how conditional expressions should be made available to the user. There are some options under ?TapeConfig, but a simpler way may be to define your own, e.g.:

max2 <- function(x,y).5*(abs(x-y)+x+y)

and then replace

pnoRet <- ifelse(pnoV1 - pnoV2 > 1e-323, pnoV1 - pnoV2, 1e-323)

by

pnoRet <- max2(pnoV1 - pnoV2, 1e-323)

To give suggestions on this I think we need to know something about the covariance matrix dimension or other structural properties that might be relevant.
Would a Monte Carlo method be feasible? FWIW, a 1D Monte Carlo version of 'pnorm' could be made like this:

mcpnorm <- function(x) {
  N <- 1e3
  u <- rnorm(N)
  sum(plogis( 10 * (x - u) )) / N
}
F <- MakeTape(mcpnorm, 0)
F <- F$atomic() ## Can now be used from other tapes with little memory usage

messages.body_plain:
Hi Buck!

I wish you were at the RTMB ICES class with us in Nanaimo, BC right now.

Try changing your map object to something like
map <- list(c(factor(1),factor(NA)))

On Mon, Feb 26, 2024 at 9:18 AM 'William Stockhausen - NOAA Federal' via TMB Users <tmb-...@googlegroups.com> wrote:

> Probably I'm doing this wrong, but I have the following very simple example for turning off estimation of specific parameters using the map function:
>
> require(RTMB);
> objfun<-function(params){
>   getAll(params);
>   y %~% dnorm(a[1]+a[2]*x,1);
> }
>
> a = c(1,2);
> x = 0:10
> y = a[1] + a[2]*x + rnorm(length(x),0,1);
> plot(x,y);
> params = list(a=a);
> map = list(a=factor(1:length(a)));
> # map$a[2] = NA;
>
> obj = MakeADFun(objfun,parameters=params,map=map);
> opt = nlminb(obj$par,obj$fn,obj$gr);
> sdr = sdreport(obj);
> summary(sdr)
>
> When I run it as above (with map$a[2] = NA; commented out), for the summary I get
>    Estimate Std. Error
> a 0.7388331 0.56407607
> a 2.1037572 0.09534626
>
> When I uncomment the `map$a[2] = NA;` line, I get the error
> Error in optimHess(par.fixed, obj$fn, obj$gr) :
>   non-finite value supplied by optim
>
> and the value for a[2] in opt$par (or obj$env$last.par), which should be fixed at 2 if I've done it right, is NA.
>
> So is this a problem with me or with RTMB?
>
> Thanks for any help!
>

Thanks for your suggestions! They both worked, but they seem a bit less general than what the MakeADFun documentation suggests you can do.

My mistake was apparently doing this:

map$a = factor(length(a)); map$a[2] = NA; (i.e., setting the NA after creating the factor)

to "fix" a[2] (which didn't work) whereas doing the following did work:

ma = 1:length(a); ma[2] = NA; map$a = factor(ma);

I.e., setting the NAs before creating the factor vector. I don't know (quite obviously) if there are other approaches, but would love to hear about them.

One thing I was a bit surprised by was that the sdreport'ed parameter values did not include the "fixed" values. However, I was able to get the "full" parameter vector after optimization (i.e., including the fixed value a[2] (with std=0)) by adding ADREPORT(a) to the objective function code.
